definition.def: If one thing indicates another, the first thing shows that the second is true or exists.
examples: A survey of retired people has indicated that most are independent and enjoying life. [VERB that]
Our vote today indicates a change in United States policy. [VERB noun]
This indicates whether remedies are suitable for children. [VERB wh]

definition.def: If you indicate an opinion, an intention, or a fact, you mention it in an indirect way.
examples: Mr Rivers has indicated that he may resign. [VERB that]
U.S. authorities have not yet indicated their monetary policy plans. [VERB noun]

definition.def: If you indicate something to someone, you show them where it is, especially by pointing to it. [formal]
examples: He indicated a chair. 'Sit down.' [VERB noun]
Pelham moved across to indicate a wall chart. [VERB noun]

definition.def: If one thing indicates something else, it is a sign of that thing.
examples: Dreams can help indicate your true feelings. [VERB noun]
His language indicates a poor education. [VERB noun]

definition.def: If a technical instrument indicates something, it shows a measurement or reading.
examples: The needles that indicate your height are at the top right-hand corner. [VERB noun]
The temperature gauge indicated that it was boiling. [VERB that]

definition.def: When drivers indicate, they make lights flash on one side of their vehicle to show that they are going to turn in that direction. [mainly British]
examples: He told us when to indicate and when to change gear. [VERB]
